definitions.explanation: A large predatory fish with cartilaginous skeleton, multiple rows of teeth, and a streamlined body.

examples.japanese: {鮫|さめ}は{海|うみ}の{食物連鎖|しょくもつれんさ}の{頂点|ちょうてん}にいる。
examples.english: Sharks are at the top of the ocean food chain.

examples.japanese: この{海岸|かいがん}では{鮫|さめ}が{出|で}ることがあるので{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Sharks sometimes appear at this beach, so caution is necessary.

examples.japanese: {鮫|さめ}は{嗅覚|きゅうかく}が{非常|ひじょう}に{発達|はったつ}している。
examples.english: Sharks have a highly developed sense of smell.

notes:
{鮫|さめ} refers to sharks in general.

Alternative writing: サメ (katakana, common in scientific contexts)

Common types:
- ホホジロ{鮫|ざめ} / ホオジロ{鮫|ざめ} (great white shark)
- ジンベエ{鮫|ざめ} (whale shark)
- シュモク{鮫|ざめ} (hammerhead shark)

Common expressions:
- {鮫|さめ}{肌|はだ} (rough skin; literally "shark skin")
- {鮫|さめ}{皮|がわ} (sharkskin, also used for sword handle wrapping)

Counter: {匹|ひき} or {頭|とう} (for large sharks)

Cultural note:
In traditional Japanese swordmaking, {鮫|さめ}{皮|がわ} (ray/shark skin) is used to wrap sword handles for grip. This material is actually from rays rather than sharks in most cases.
